clue.text: Graduates only on 2/11?

definitions.meaning: ... College, Oxford, has fellows but no undergraduate students, so it admits graduates only
the second of November, the Christian day for commemorating the faithful departed

explanation.walkthrough: Read 2/11 the British way, day before month: 2 November, not 11 February.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses name the same thing: an Oxford college with only graduate members, and the November feast for the dead.

clue.text: 7-6 dessert wine?

parts.note: afters is British informal for the pudding course
hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A sweet wine served after dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 7-6 is the linked answer's first two words, POST-TRAUMATIC: a later tremor following an earthquake, or a delayed reaction after a blow, comes after the trauma.
explanation.definitionFit: A further tremor or delayed reaction comes after the initial event, so it is literally a post-trauma happening.

clue.text: Confectionery for the world (not English — Europe's bits)

indicators.note: not here means take away, so the letter for English goes from each piece

parts.note: le monde is French for the world, a European tongue rather than English

indicators.note: bits of a word are runs of its letters, here a run inside the word Europe's

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English, here dropped once from each piece

explanation.surface: Sweets on sale everywhere, though the label is continental, not English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not English' takes E out of both pieces: LEMONDE loses one to give LEMOND, and ROPES, a run of letters in Europe's, loses one to give ROPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemon drops are small boiled sweets flavoured with lemon, a kind of confectionery.

clue.text: Fabric for Londoners' use

indicators.note: the letters are put to use from within the words for Londoners', running across the gap

explanation.surface: A cloth made specially for people in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Orlon is a trade name for an acrylic fibre and the fabric woven from it.

clue.text: Pink as heart to heart?

definitions.meaning: pink describes someone mildly left-wing in politics, not fully red
the heart organ sits slightly to the left of the middle, or heart, of the chest

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense plays on heart meaning both the organ and the centre of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild socialist views are politically moderate leftism, and the heart's position in the chest is just off the midline to the left.

clue.text: Silly little boy eating mutton

indicators.note: one piece eats the other, taking it inside itself

parts.note: Sid is a short form of the boy's name Sidney
a tup is a ram, so loosely a source of mutton

explanation.surface: A foolish child tucking into a lamb dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Silly and foolish are close synonyms describing a lack of sense.

clue.text: See 7
Disorder for order, crackling with tension about most of 20's dream

parts.note: PO is short for postal order

indicators.note: the crackling word goes about, surrounding, the German word

parts.note: static is the crackling noise on a radio or phone line
20 is GERMAN BIGHT; most of it is the word German, and Traum is German for dream
stress is mental or physical tension

explanation.surface: A muddled request about crackly noise and anxiety in a dream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'with' are links. The tricky bit is 'most of 20's dream': 20 is GERMAN BIGHT, so most of it is GERMAN, and a German's word for dream is TRAUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Post-traumatic stress is a recognised psychiatric condition following a terrible experience, so it is a disorder.

clue.text: When it's a stone

definitions.meaning: a palm fruit with a stone at its centre

explanation.definitionFit: The calendar sense answers the question when, and the fruit sense is a stone fruit from the date palm.

clue.text: Inversion of all one's days by periodical corporation

indicators.note: inversion here swaps the two halves of the phrase so the second comes first

parts.note: all the days of one's existence make up one's lifetime

explanation.surface: Turning upside down a whole life spent working for a magazine company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inversion of' swaps LIFE and TIME rather than reversing the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Time-Life was the American publishing company behind Time and Life magazines, a corporation of periodicals.

clue.text: Dog, 5 creature, in speculation

indicators.note: the creature goes in the middle of the wager word

parts.note: a bet is a speculation on an outcome
5 is STUPID, and a stupid creature is an ass

explanation.surface: A dog, a daft animal, caught up in a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A basset is a short-legged hound with long ears, a breed of dog.

clue.text: One providing care and training that's for free

indicators.note: training puts the letters through drills until they form new ranks

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after and teaches a child without charging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link; the apostrophe of that's is no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who brings up a child not his own provides parental care, a definition by description.

clue.text: Start functioning well, show keenness at 24, or collide with 25

definitions.meaning: to come into form, as a player or team hitting their stride
24 is SCHOOL, where a form is a class, so a keen pupil hurries into it
25 is THE BENCH, and a form is also a long bench, so one can bump into it

explanation.walkthrough: Three senses: form as good condition, as a school class, and as a bench seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Each reading is the same phrase: reaching good form, rushing into a classroom, or bumping into a bench.

clue.text: Brahminist 'aving left information for church's gratification

indicators.note: having with its H dropped, telling us to drop the H of the believer too

parts.note: a follower of Brahminism is a Hindu
gen is British slang for information
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A Hindu dropping his aitches has left news about church pleasures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. 'aving shows an H dropped, as in Cockney speech, so HINDU becomes INDU.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence is the giving way to a desire, i.e. pleasure or gratification.

clue.text: Unnatural problem with right hand affected

indicators.note: a problem leaves the letters in trouble, jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: A medical complaint: the right hand is impaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link: R and H join the letters of affected to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something far-fetched is implausible or strained, so unnatural in the sense of contrived.

clue.text: Water supply about right for the one you can take to it

definitions.text: the one you can take to it

indicators.note: the water-supply word goes about, around, the letter

parts.note: a hose supplies water

explanation.surface: A garden hose near the right animal to lead to a trough.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition recalls the proverb: you can lead a horse to water but you can't make it drink; 'it' is the water.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb names this animal as the creature you can lead to water but not make drink.

clue.text: Outstandingly bad (say) royal without love

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

indicators.note: without means outside, so the royal word goes round the love letter

parts.note: regius means royal, as in a Regius professor
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A dreadful king who has no love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, not lacking: REGIUS goes round O to make REGIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Egregious means shockingly bad, from the Latin for standing out from the flock.

clue.text: Change of heart in European region brings liability to trance

indicators.note: the heart of the region's name, its central letter, is changed for another

parts.note: Catalonia is a region of north-east Spain

explanation.surface: A political turnaround in a Spanish region makes people dreamy.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of CATALONIA is L; change it to T.
explanation.definitionFit: Catatonia is a state of stupor or immobility, so a proneness to trance-like states.

clue.text: Dick painting fiddler misses nothing — he's not alone

parts.note: dick is slang for a detective, a cop
painting is art

indicators.note: the fiddler misses, lacks, the nothing letter

parts.note: Nero supposedly fiddled while Rome burned
O is nothing, zero

explanation.surface: Dick paints and fiddles, minus the zero, and has company.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero, the Roman emperor, is the proverbial fiddler while Rome burned.
explanation.definitionFit: A copartner shares a business with another, so is by definition not acting alone.

clue.text: Sound like a steam-engine to make one happy?

definitions.meaning: to puff rhythmically like a locomotive
British slang: to be pleased, so this makes one glad

explanation.definitionFit: The verb names the puffing noise of a steam train, and in British slang it also means to please.

clue.text: Fisher's neighbour, cause of illness to other than swollen inside

parts.note: a germ causes disease

indicators.note: the swollen word goes inside the reworked letters
other means the word than is made different, its letters rearranged

parts.note: big can mean swollen

explanation.surface: A germ causes illness for someone who isn't swollen inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. 'other' makes ANHT from than; 'inside' puts BIG into it: AN-BIG-HT. Fisher and German Bight are neighbouring sea areas in the BBC Shipping Forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: German Bight is a sea area adjoining Fisher in the British shipping forecast, so is its neighbour.

clue.text: Not hard work following live music

indicators.note: the soft and work pieces follow the live word

parts.note: to be is to live
B marks a soft pencil lead, the opposite of H for hard
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Gentle work coming after a live music show.
explanation.walkthrough: Pencil leads are graded H for hard and B for soft and black.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop is a style of fast, complex jazz from the 1940s, a kind of music.

clue.text: Goddess of river …

definitions.meaning: the Egyptian goddess of magic and motherhood
the name for the Thames as it flows through Oxford

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link; the dots lead into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both an Egyptian deity and the Oxford stretch of the River Thames.

clue.text: … even if river wants god

parts.note: tho is an informal spelling of though, meaning even if

explanation.surface: A river lacking a god, carrying on from the goddess above.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder.

clue.text: Classes of fish?

parts.note: lessons for the young read as a group of swimmers moving together

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a place of classes and a large group of fish swimming together.

clue.text: Fish swallowing Hebrew judges

indicators.note: the fish swallows, taking in, the short form of Hebrew

parts.note: the tench is a freshwater fish
Heb is the abbreviation for Hebrew

explanation.surface: A fish gulping down a Hebrew scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: The bench is the collective term for judges or magistrates.

clue.text: See 7
Rude remark to gorgeous or 5 creature

definitions.meaning: a blunt dismissal telling someone to go away and die
the phrase goes before gorgeous, as in stunningly good-looking, and with the inserted it goes around a stupid creature, the donkey of the TV comedy title

explanation.walkthrough: 5 is STUPID, so the creature is a donkey: Drop the Dead Donkey was a 1990s British sitcom set in a TV newsroom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is an insult on its own, an intensifier before 'gorgeous', and part of a British sitcom title.
